soundness_flags.label: ass:latent-a0-transport-support and ass:latent-a1-transport-support
soundness_flags.one_line: These target-relevant cross-world transport restrictions are not the standard WBC positivity condition cited; Wu--Bai--Cui state global observed mediator/hidden-witness support, so retag them novel with a substantive applicability justification or provide a source for this exact restricted condition.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 1 / ass:latent-valid-bridge-existence
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The broad identification result is conditional on existence of a bridge vector that is both latent-valid and solves the observed coupled system; that intersection is assumed, not derived over the full class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Point identification conditional on latent-valid sequential bridge realizability and RI(P); Proposition 2 provides only a sufficient subfamily.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The source requires global treatment and mediator positivity in Assumption 2.1, gives proxy exclusions and observed bridge equations in Assumptions 3.1 and 3.3, uses completeness in Assumption 3.2 to derive the latent bridge equations in Proposition 3.1, and identifies the hidden-recanting target in Theorem 3.1.

The published article studies counterfactual-mean identification and inference with nonunique proximal bridge solutions, including conditions for uniquely defined linear functionals and root-n estimation.

Version 4 has the four listed authors and derives incomplete-proxy partial-identification methods, including analogous hidden-mediator results, without point identification of the bridge or causal effect.
The article identifies causal effects using at least two independent proxy variables satisfying a rank condition and treats failure of that condition as a limitation.
The paper establishes strong identification and root-n inference for linear functionals despite weakly identified, potentially nonunique nuisance functions under additional conditions.
The source is the three-author proximal-mediation paper corresponding to the cited 2023 Biometrika article.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag the two target-relevant latent transport conditions as novel and explain empirically when their restricted support is defensible; alternatively derive them from an explicitly stated primitive sampling/structural condition.

Add a generic nonidentification region or a proved restricted converse beyond the single counterpair, so failure of RI has causal—not merely affine-fiber—content on an open WBC subclass.
